name: 1 - Freelance design and copywriting agreement.pdf
text:
Independent Contractor Services Agreement This Independent Contractor Services Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made on 2 November 2026 (the “Effective Date”) between Larkspur Media Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Client”), and Jordan Ellis, an individual trading as Ellis Studio (“Contractor”).
1. Services
1.1 Contractor will provide the brand design, copywriting and content production services described in each statement of work signed by both parties (each a “Statement of Work”).
Each Statement of Work forms part of this Agreement.
1.2 Contractor will decide how, when and where the Services are performed, and will supply Contractor’s own equipment and software.
1.3 Deliverables will be shared through a cloud folder named for the project, which Client will set up and give Contractor access to.
1.4 Contractor will make any revisions Client requests to a Deliverable until Client approves it, at no additional charge.
2. Fees and payment
2.1 Client will pay Contractor the fees set out in Schedule A for each Deliverable that Client accepts.
2.2 Contractor will invoice Client at the end of each calendar month for Deliverables accepted in that month.
2.3 Client will pay each undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days of receiving it, and Client may dispute any invoice in its sole discretion, in which case the disputed amount is not payable until the dispute is resolved.
2.4 If a Deliverable is delivered after its due date, the fee for that Deliverable is reduced by ten percent (10%) for each week or part of a week of delay.
2.5 Client may set off against any amount it owes Contractor any amount that Contractor owes Client or any affiliate of Client, under this Agreement or under any other agreement.
2.6 Client will reimburse reasonable travel expenses that Client has approved in writing in advance, within thirty (30) days of receiving the receipts.
3. Term and termination
3.1 This Agreement starts on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6)
months (the “Initial Term”).

3.2 At the end of the Initial Term and of each renewal term, this Agreement continues for a further six (6) month term unless Contractor gives notice to end it at least sixty (60) days before the term then running ends, and the fees for each renewal term are the fees in Schedule A as Client adjusts them by notice at the start of that term.
3.3 Client may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work at any time and for any reason by written notice, and Client will owe nothing for work in progress that Client has not accepted on the date of the notice.
3.4 Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure the breach within thirty (30) days of receiving notice describing it.
4. Intellectual property
4.1 Contractor assigns to Client all right, title and interest in every Deliverable and in all materials, tools, templates, methods and know-how that Contractor used to create it, including anything Contractor created before the Effective Date.
4.2 Contractor waives any moral rights Contractor may have in the Deliverables, to the extent the law allows.
4.3 Contractor may show finished Deliverables in Contractor’s portfolio once Client has published them.
5. Restrictions after the Agreement ends
5.1 For twelve (12) months after this Agreement ends for any reason, Contractor will not provide design, copywriting or content services to any business that competes with Client or with any customer of Client — whether as an employee, a contractor or on Contractor’s own account.
5.2 Neither party will, during this Agreement, hire an employee of the other party who worked on the Services without the other party’s written consent.
6. Confidentiality
6.1 Each party will keep the other party’s confidential information confidential, will use it only to perform this Agreement, and will return or destroy it when this Agreement ends.
6.2 Confidential information does not include information that is public through no fault of the receiving party, or that the receiving party already knew or developed on its own.
7. Indemnification and liability
7.1 Contractor will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Client and its officers, employees and affiliates against any claim, loss, liability or expense, including reasonable legal fees,

arising out of or relating to the Services or the Deliverables, including any claim arising from materials that Client supplied to Contractor.
7.2 Client’s total liability to Contractor for any claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the fees Client paid to Contractor in the three (3) months before the event giving rise to the claim, and this limit does not apply to any liability of Contractor.
7.3 Contractor will maintain professional liability insurance with cover of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per claim for the whole of this Agreement and for three (3)
years after it ends, and will provide a certificate of that insurance on request.
8. Changes to this Agreement
8.1 Client may update the Vendor Guidelines and the terms of this Agreement from time to time by posting a revised version on the Larkspur vendor portal, and the revised version applies to Contractor from the date it is posted.
8.2 Contractor will follow the Vendor Guidelines in force from time to time.
9. Disputes
9.1 Any dispute between the parties arising out of this Agreement will be resolved by binding arbitration before a single arbitrator in Wilmington, Delaware, and each party will bear its own costs of the arbitration.
9.2 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
10. General
10.1 Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee of Client, and is responsible for Contractor’s own taxes.
10.2 Each party will send notices under this Agreement to the email address shown for the other party on the signature page.
10.3 Contractor will use Client’s brand colour palette, which Client will provide on request, in all mock-ups.
10.4 This Agreement, with its Schedules and Statements of Work, is the whole agreement between the parties about its subject.

summary: You (Jordan Ellis, trading as Ellis Studio) will provide brand design, copywriting and content production services to Larkspur Media Group, Inc. under statements of work, deciding yourself how, when and where the work is done and supplying your own equipment. You will be paid the fees in Schedule A — for example $6,500 for a brand identity package, $450 per page of website copy and $1,800 per month for social media content — for deliverables Client accepts, invoiced monthly and paid within ninety days, with Client able to dispute invoices at its sole discretion, and with fees reduced 10% per week for late delivery. Client may also offset anything you owe it or its affiliates against payments due to you, and will reimburse pre-approved travel expenses. The agreement runs for an initial six-month term and renews automatically for six-month terms unless you give at least sixty days' notice; Client may end it at any time for any reason without paying for unaccepted work in progress, and either party may end it for uncured material breach. You assign to Client all rights in every deliverable and in the materials, tools and know-how used to create them, waive your moral rights, and may show finished work in your portfolio only once Client has published it. For twelve months after the agreement ends you may not provide design, copywriting or content services to any business that competes with Client or any of its customers, and you must indemnify Client against claims arising from your services, carry $2 million professional liability insurance during the term and for three years after, while Client's liability to you is capped at fees paid in the prior three months. Client can change the agreement's terms and the Vendor Guidelines by posting updates on its vendor portal, and disputes go to binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware under Delaware law.

flags.sourceSentence: Client may update the Vendor Guidelines and the terms of this Agreement from time to time by posting a revised version on the Larkspur vendor portal, and the revised version applies to Contractor from the date it is posted.
flags.explanation: Larkspur can rewrite the terms of this agreement and its guidelines at any time, and the new version binds you from the moment it appears on its vendor portal — you never have to agree or even be told directly.

flags.clauseType: IP assignment covering tools and pre-existing work
flags.sourceSentence: Contractor assigns to Client all right, title and interest in every Deliverable and in all materials, tools, templates, methods and know-how that Contractor used to create it, including anything Contractor created before the Effective Date.
flags.explanation: You assign Larkspur your reusable templates, tools and methods and even work you created before signing, so your studio's own assets leave with the deliverables.

readings: You hand over ownership not just of the deliverables but of your own templates, methods and know-how, including material you made before signing.

You hand over ownership of the deliverables and of any tools or templates you used on them, and the pre-existing-date phrase reaches back only to work created before the Effective Date that went into them.
ambiguity.hedge: This sentence could be read two ways. One reading: You hand over ownership not just of the deliverables but of your own templates, methods and know-how, including material you made before signing. The other: You hand over ownership of the deliverables and of any tools or templates you used on them, and the pre-existing-date phrase reaches back only to work created before the Effective Date that went into them.

flags.sourceSentence:
Contractor will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Client and its officers, employees and affiliates against any claim, loss, liability or expense, including reasonable legal fees,

arising out of or relating to the Services or the Deliverables, including any claim arising from materials that Client supplied to Contractor.
flags.explanation: You must pay Larkspur's legal costs and losses for almost any claim connected to your work — even claims caused by materials Larkspur itself gave you.

flags.clauseType: Termination for convenience with no payment for work in progress
flags.sourceSentence: Client may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work at any time and for any reason by written notice, and Client will owe nothing for work in progress that Client has not accepted on the date of the notice.
flags.explanation: Larkspur can end the agreement or any statement of work at any moment for any reason, and everything you have produced but not yet had accepted is unpaid — you carry the full cost of work in progress.

flags.clauseType: 90-day payment terms and discretionary invoice disputes
flags.sourceSentence: Client will pay each undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days of receiving it, and Client may dispute any invoice in its sole discretion, in which case the disputed amount is not payable until the dispute is resolved.
flags.explanation: You wait ninety days for money you have already earned, and Larkspur alone can freeze payment of any invoice simply by calling it disputed.

flags.clauseType: Automatic renewal with fees set by Client
flags.sourceSentence: At the end of the Initial Term and of each renewal term, this Agreement continues for a further six (6) month term unless Contractor gives notice to end it at least sixty (60) days before the term then running ends, and the fees for each renewal term are the fees in Schedule A as Client adjusts them by notice at the start of that term.
flags.explanation: The agreement renews itself, and at the start of each renewal term Larkspur can set your fees to whatever it announces, while you must give sixty days' notice to stop it.

flags.sourceSentence: Contractor will make any revisions Client requests to a Deliverable until Client approves it, at no additional charge.
flags.explanation: Larkspur can keep demanding changes to a deliverable indefinitely, and you are never paid for any of that work, since only accepted deliverables earn fees.

flags.sourceSentence: If a Deliverable is delivered after its due date, the fee for that Deliverable is reduced by ten percent (10%) for each week or part of a week of delay.
flags.explanation: Every week of delay cuts your fee by ten percent with no floor, so a deliverable that slips a few weeks earns you little or nothing for work already done.

flags.clauseType: Insurance obligation lasting three years after the agreement
flags.sourceSentence:
Contractor will maintain professional liability insurance with cover of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000) per claim for the whole of this Agreement and for three (3)
years after it ends, and will provide a certificate of that insurance on request.
flags.explanation: You must keep two million dollars of professional liability cover — and keep paying premiums for it — for three years after the agreement has ended.

flags.sourceSentence: Client may set off against any amount it owes Contractor any amount that Contractor owes Client or any affiliate of Client, under this Agreement or under any other agreement.
flags.explanation: Larkspur can withhold money it owes you here to cover a claimed debt from a completely separate agreement with any company in its group, without your consent.

flags.sourceSentence: Contractor waives any moral rights Contractor may have in the Deliverables, to the extent the law allows.
flags.explanation: You permanently give up the right to be credited or to object to how your work is altered, at no benefit to you.

gaps.statement: This agreement sets no deadline or criteria for the Client to accept or reject a Deliverable, so acceptance can be withheld indefinitely even though fees are only owed for accepted work.
gaps.explanation: You are paid per Deliverable the Client accepts, but nothing in the agreement says how quickly the Client must review a Deliverable, what standard it is judged against, or what happens if the Client neither accepts nor rejects it. The Client can leave your work in limbo and you have no right to be paid for it.

gaps.statement: This agreement imposes no consequence on the Client for paying late, even though payment is not due until ninety days after invoicing and the Client can extend that further by disputing an invoice in its sole discretion.
gaps.explanation: If Larkspur simply does not pay your undisputed invoice, the agreement gives you no interest, surcharge, or other remedy, and nothing accelerates payment. Ninety days is the floor of your wait, not a deadline the Client risks anything by missing.

gaps.statement: This agreement caps the Client's total liability to you but sets no cap at all on your total liability to the Client or on the indemnity you give the Client.
gaps.explanation: Larkspur's exposure is limited to three months of fees, but your indemnity covers claims arising from the Services, the Deliverables, and even materials Larkspur itself supplied, with no dollar ceiling. A single claim could exceed everything you earn under this agreement.

gaps.statement: This agreement provides no process or timeline for resolving a disputed invoice, so an amount the Client disputes in its sole discretion can sit unpaid indefinitely.
gaps.explanation: Larkspur can dispute any invoice for any reason, the disputed amount is not payable until the dispute is resolved, and the agreement says nothing about how it gets resolved. You have no route to force a decision on whether the money is owed.

gaps.statement: This agreement reduces your fee for late delivery of a Deliverable even when the delay was caused by the Client.
gaps.explanation: The fee reduction applies automatically to any Deliverable delivered after its due date, and the agreement nowhere relieves you of delay caused by Larkspur — for example, late feedback, late supply of materials, or the cloud folder not being set up. You bear the cost of the Client's own delays.

gaps.statement: This agreement gives you no right to stop work or end the agreement mid-term if the Client does not pay you.
gaps.explanation: Outside the breach-and-cure process, which gives the Client thirty days to cure even a failure to pay, you cannot suspend the Services or leave before the current six-month term runs out. You must keep working while payment is outstanding.

gaps.statement: This agreement says nothing about who owns or may use Contractor's pre-existing tools and templates after they are assigned to the Client.
gaps.explanation: You assign all tools, templates, methods and know-how used to create Deliverables, including anything you made before the Effective Date, and the agreement gives you no licence back. You cannot keep using your own prior work in future projects for other clients.
